sources.title: Sahih al-Bukhari 1166: The prayer and supplication of Istikhara
sources.supports: Jabir narrates two non-obligatory rakahs followed by the supplication, naming the matter. The Arabic includes facilitation and blessing, unlike the shorter wording in 6382; it records two alternative phrases about the outcome.

sources.title: Dar al-Ifta: Istikhara prayer and its results
sources.supports: The institution describes two voluntary rakahs outside prohibited prayer times, specifying the contemplated choice when making dua, and entrusting its outcome to Allah.

sources.title: Dar al-Ifta: How to recognize the result of Istikhara
sources.supports: A dream or a feeling of pleasure is not necessary after Istikhara; the answer discusses whether the matter becomes possible.

review.notes: Compared the actual Arabic of Bukhari 6382 and 1166. Cited 1166 for the full wording including facilitation and blessing; retained one narrated alternative rather than concatenating variants. English meaning is independently phrased from Arabic. Dar al-Ifta captures support method and absence of required dreams/feelings. Removed unsupported repeat-count and outcome certainty claims; practical examples are explicitly editorial. Three headings with no redundant FAQs; existing title/date/authors/image path preserved, title-placeholder image replaced by user-authorized generated artwork.
